name: Bayern Munich 1973/74-1975/76 (three European Cups)
scopeNote: Bayern Munich across 1973/74, 1974/75 and 1975/76, winners of the European Cup in 1974 (Atletico Madrid, 1-1 and 4-0 replay), 1975 (Leeds 2-0) and 1976 (Saint-Etienne 1-0). Udo Lattek coached to January 1975, Dettmar Cramer from 16 January 1975. Period start (first Bundesliga match, 25 Aug 1973) and end (end of 1975/76 season) are approximate boundaries: the exact first and last match dates were not verified in a read page. The 1976 Intercontinental Cup (Nov-Dec 1976, under Cramer) falls in 1976/77 and is excluded. Sources describe Beckenbauer as an attacking libero/sweeper in a still man-marking era (Champions Journal: 'strict man-marking'); the often-repeated 'Total Football' label for this Bayern is a Glanville-attributed claim, not a source-backed Dutch-style system. Tactical coverage is thin: the 1975 final is the only match with a tactical account, and it is atypical (Bayern deliberately defensive, Mueller deep). Cramer's and Lattek's own words on tactics were not found.
openQuestions: Lattek end date: DFB Datencenter (search summary only, not read) gives 1975-01-02; Wikipedia gives only 'January 1975'. Cramer start 16 Jan 1975 verified (Wikipedia).
Period start 1973-08-25 is from memory and unverified; confirm Bayern's first 1973/74 competitive match.
Marking: UEFA FR (unread) says Cramer and Lattek used individual marking in a 1-3-3-3 with Beckenbauer as libero; only one source, unverified. Zonal vs man not otherwise confirmed.
Whether the 1975 final (Mueller as defensive midfielder, Bayern sitting deep) reflects Cramer's usual approach or a one-off plan for Leeds is unclear.
Wikipedia says Cramer was criticised for a 'passive management style'; no other source corroborates.
Lattek-Cramer attribution of the 1974-76 style: FourFourTwo and Champions Journal credit Beckenbauer more than either coach.

sources.title: Der Kaiser (Champions Journal)
sources.evidence: Their maestro was their sweeper, or more precisely: their libero. Because Beckenbauer had done what almost nobody else had ever done – he had invented a new role on the field for himself, in the process changing his team’s entire approach to the game. Beckenbauer wasn’t content with sweeping up at the back, unlike his counterparts in Italy, where the libero position had been pioneered. Instead, he regularly dashed forward across the midfield line

sources.title: Udo Lattek, Wikipedia
sources.evidence: A poor start to the 1974–75 domestic season saw Lattek's tenure come to an end, with Bayern replacing him with Dettmar Cramer, who was also recommended to the club by Beckenbauer. According to Lattek, after telling club president Wilhelm Neudecker that, given the club's poor domestic form changes were necessary, Neudecker replied, "Correct. You're sacked."

sources.title: How Beckenbauer became the brains, guts and vision of Bayern Munich, FourFourTwo
sources.evidence: Between 1974 and 1976, Bayern became the third team to win three successive European Cups. Although the Roten’s treble was achieved under the management of Dettmar Cramer and Udo Lattek, you could make a case that Beckenbauer, directing play as the sweeper, was the true architect of that golden era.

sources.title: How Beckenbauer became the brains, guts and vision of Bayern Munich, FourFourTwo

He did, and total football was born at Bayern Munich.”
